# `Q-1-10` — Missing Required Property

> A YAML document is missing a property that its schema marks as
> required.

## What this means

Quarto's configuration files (such as `_quarto.yml`) and many of
its metadata blocks follow schemas that define which properties
must appear. This error fires when your YAML omits a required
property: schema validation rejects the document, and Quarto
refuses to proceed.

The error names the missing property and the location of the
surrounding YAML object — the place in the file where the
property should appear.

## Why this happens

The three common causes:

- **The property is genuinely missing.** You started a
  configuration block but did not fill in every required field
  before saving.
- **The property name is misspelled.** What you intended as the
  required property landed under a typo, so the schema does not
  see it.
- **You copied an incomplete example.** A snippet that worked in
  another context was not, on its own, a complete configuration
  for the schema it landed in.

## How to fix

Add the missing property at the same nesting level the schema
expects, then re-run Quarto. The error message shows both the
property name and the path inside the YAML where it belongs, so
the place to add it is unambiguous.

If the property looks present but the error still fires, check the
spelling carefully — YAML key names are case-sensitive, and a
required `title` will not be satisfied by `Title` or `titel`.

If the schema's requirement looks wrong for your case, consult the
Quarto documentation for the configuration block in question. A
property is required because something downstream cannot run
without it; the documentation should explain why.

## Example

A `_quarto.yml` declares a website but omits the `title` property:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website

website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
```

Running `quarto render` reports the missing `title` and points at
the `website` block where it should appear.

Fix the configuration by adding the required property at the
correct nesting level:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My Site"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
```

## Related

- `Q-1-11` — type mismatch: the property is present, but its value
  has the wrong type.
- `Q-1-18` — unknown property: a property is present but the
  schema does not recognize it (often a typo of a different
  required property).

Cross-references render as plain code spans until the target pages
